title: "Research"
subtitle: "Experimental and numerical mechanics of advanced materials"

My research is developed within the **COMES — Mecánica de los Medios Continuos, Ingeniería de Estructuras y de Materiales** research group at the University of Castilla-La Mancha. The common thread is the mechanical response of materials and structures under complex loading, combining advanced experiments with analytical and numerical modelling.

[COMES research group](https://www.uclm.es/grupos/COMES)

```{=html}

  <article class="research-block">

      <h3>Multiaxial testing</h3>
      <p>Design and interpretation of biaxial and multiaxial tests, particularly with cruciform specimens. Current work includes tension–tension, tension–compression and compression-dominated load states, specimen stability and full-field strain measurement.</p>
      <div class="method-line">DIC · strain gauges · cruciform specimens · instability analysis</div>

  <article class="research-block">

    <div class="research-block-copy">
      <div class="eyebrow">Composite mechanics</div>
      <h3>Non-linear response of CFRP laminates</h3>
      <p>Study of symmetric angle-ply laminates whose response is strongly governed by in-plane shear, including pseudo-ductility, fibre reorientation, damage accumulation and the transition between different response stages.</p>
      <div class="method-line">angle-ply CFRP · pseudo-ductility · non-linearity · failure</div>
    </div>
  </article>

  <article class="research-block">

    <div class="research-block-copy">
      <div class="eyebrow">Computational mechanics</div>
      <h3>Damage and failure modelling</h3>
      <p>Finite-element simulation at different scales, from representative fibre–matrix models to laminate-level damage formulations. Abaqus is used to analyse initiation, stiffness degradation, crack propagation and failure under multiaxial loading.</p>
      <div class="method-line">Abaqus · FEM/XFEM · micro/mesoscale · progressive damage</div>
    </div>

      <h3>Measurement & inverse interpretation</h3>
      <p>Integration of Digital Image Correlation with mechanical testing to obtain heterogeneous strain fields, identify local phenomena and support the validation or inverse identification of numerical models.</p>
      <div class="method-line">2D/3D DIC · full-field strain · model validation</div>
```

## Shear characterisation and standardisation

```{=html}
<div class="shear-showcase">
  <div class="shear-main-image">
    <img src="assets/photos/une-biaxial-test.jpg" alt="Biaxial tension-compression shear test using a cruciform specimen and dedicated fixture.">
  </div>
  <div class="shear-main-copy">
    <div class="eyebrow">Highlighted methodology</div>
    <h3>Biaxial tension–compression test · UNE 0074:2023</h3>
    <p>A central line of work is the determination of in-plane shear properties by means of a biaxial tension–compression test with a cruciform specimen. The methodology developed within COMES contributed to <strong>UNE 0074:2023</strong> and to the BISHEAR proof-of-concept project.</p>
    <p>The test is analysed together with conventional shear methods in order to compare the stress/strain state, experimental accessibility and suitability for advanced composite characterisation.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="mini-method-grid standards-grid">

  </div>
```

## Experimental and numerical capabilities

```{=html}
<div class="card-grid">
  <div class="info-card"><h3>Experimental</h3><p>Quasi-static mechanical testing, biaxial loading, DIC, extensometry, composite specimens and structural test design.</p></div>
  <div class="info-card"><h3>Numerical</h3><p>Abaqus/FEA, non-linear mechanics, damage modelling, buckling and stability, micro/mesoscale simulations.</p></div>
  <div class="info-card"><h3>Materials</h3><p>Carbon-fibre reinforced polymer laminates, polymer systems, nanocomposites, lightweight structures and selected additively manufactured materials.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Collaboration

My doctoral research included a three-month research stay at **Ghent University** in 2019, focused on micro- and mesomechanical damage modelling of angle-ply laminates under uniaxial and biaxial loading.

For collaboration proposals related to composite testing, numerical modelling or multiaxial mechanics, see the [contact page](contact.html).
